mission_1.search: BFS and A* both found a shortest path of 13.5 m. BFS expanded 928 nodes, while A* expanded 700 nodes, so A* examined 228 fewer cells. My BFS implementation uses a FIFO queue to explore cells in layers. My A* implementation uses a heap ordered by the cost so far plus the Manhattan-distance heuristic, which helps guide the search toward the goal. However, A* took about 9.34 ms, compared with 6.99 ms for BFS. Examining fewer cells did not make it faster in this run.
mission_1.failure:
On the constrained map, BFS found a 24.5 m path and expanded 848 nodes. DFS found a much longer 104 m path but expanded only 524 nodes. My DFS implementation uses a stack and follows deeper branches first, so it can reach the goal without finding the shortest route. IDDFS reached the expansion budget and returned resource_limit. On the unreachable map, BFS, DFS, IDDFS, and A all returned no_path. This means they exhausted the search without finding a route. In contrast, resource_limit means the search stopped because it reached a time limit.
I used AI to help with the writing of the four implementations, and I ran the full evaluation and inspected the resulting metrics and route plots.
